isinstance(outcome, RenderedPage) discriminates the closed owned union RenderedPage | RefusedPage that _render_page returns (both frozen dataclasses defined in elspeth.plugins.infrastructure.rasterize.protocol, Tier 1). The nominal check against the concrete owned class is ADR-032's prescribed internal-boundary form: the class object is the credential, so no pypdfium2 object or duck-typed impostor can be routed into the rendered tuple. It is not a shape guard over the external PDF — that parse already happened inside _render_page, which converts every pdfium failure into a RefusedPage value. Removing the check would require collapsing the union into a single tagged type for one call site, which is churn with no gain in integrity.
plugins/infrastructure/telemetry.py:R4:e: except Exception after an explicit `except contract_errors.TIER_1_ERRORS: raise` is the documented telemetry-delivery seam: emit_resource_cleanup_failed is called from resource cleanup paths (sink/source close, client teardown) where the original cleanup failure is already being reported, and a second failure inside the telemetry SINK (a closed emitter, a serialization fault in a subscriber) must not mask or replace the primary failure that the caller is about to raise or record. The handler is not silent — it logs a structured warning with component, resource, and error_type — and Tier-1 invariant violations plus process-control exceptions (BaseException subclasses outside Exception) re-raise through the preceding arm, which test_cleanup_telemetry_does_not_suppress_unsuppressible_failures pins per failure type. The value being protected is the audit record of the ORIGINAL cleanup failure.

isinstance(target, nodes.NSRef) is a nominal check against jinja2's concrete NSRef node class on an Assign/AssignBlock target that jinja2's parser types as Name | NSRef | Tuple | ... (`{% set ns.attr = v %}` produces NSRef). The analyzer runs on jinja2's parsed AST of an operator-authored template; the class dispatch is the same mechanism jinja2's NodeVisitor uses for every other node kind in this analyzer (visit_<Class>), applied here to an assignment TARGET, which NodeVisitor's visit() would otherwise treat as a load and mis-record. An NSRef target is a load of the namespace name (`ns` must already be bound), so the check is what turns `{% set ns.a = 1 %}` without a prior `{% set ns = namespace() %}` into a preflight-detected unbound name (test id namespace-unbound-nsref).

isinstance(target, nodes.Name) is a nominal check against jinja2's concrete Name node class on an assignment target that may be a bare Name or a compound target (Tuple/List of Names for `{% for a, b in pairs %}`). jinja2's Node.find_all deliberately excludes the receiver node itself, so the bare-Name case must be handled by this check before falling through to find_all(nodes.Name) for compound targets; every yielded node is then filtered on ctx in {'param','store'} so a load-context Name inside a target expression is never recorded as a binding. The value is jinja2's parsed AST (not ELSPETH-owned); this is class dispatch on a third-party AST, the same form the visitor uses throughout, not a shape guard hiding a contract violation.
